Scout (AI assistant)

Scout (formerly AI Advisor) is a chat assistant for WAF false-positive triage, Lua drafting and searching device configuration history — read-only by construction, with local or external AI providers configured by an administrator.

👤 ForOperatorAdministrator
🔑 Permissionsadvisor.use advisor.configure studio.lua_studio protection.edit
📍 WhereOperations → Troubleshooting → Scout (every ADOM), URL /advisor/; configuration in Settings → AI → Scout → Providers

What is it?#

Scout is the AI chat assistant built into SATOM. Operators use it to ask whether a WAF block looks like a false positive and what exception would fix it, to draft a Lua script for FortiWeb or FortiADC, and to search the stored device configuration history. It is read-only: the model cannot change SATOM or an appliance. When it proposes a change, the proposal becomes a draft that a person must apply — with the same permission the manual form requires.

ℹ️Note

Renamed on 2026-10-14: this assistant was called AI Advisor until then. The fault-localisation ladder that used to be called Scout is now Path Diagnostics. Only labels changed: the URL /advisor/, the permission keys advisor.use / advisor.configure and the audit actions advisor.* are the same.

What does it do?#

  • Chat with a configured AI provider. Replies stream in as they are generated; Stop cancels generation.
  • Attach context: the paperclip menu attaches an appliance's exception list (Exceptions — <appliance>) to the next message.
  • Read-only tools (optional): the model may look up appliances, cached server policies, device health, monitors, configuration-change history, a configuration search, exceptions and Lua scripts by itself.
  • Proposals: when the model suggests a WAF exception or a Lua script in the required format, a card appears with Apply as draft and Dismiss.
  • Per-reply accounting: each reply shows its duration, token counts (or tokens not reported) and which tools it used.
  • Attack Search integration: Attack Search can ask Scout to judge one attack-log entry or one of its fields (see Attack search).

Requirements#

All of the following, set by an administrator under Settings → System → Scout:

  1. Enable Scout switched on (off on a new installation).
  2. At least one enabled provider. Opening Settings → AI → Scout → Providers (or the Scout page) when no provider exists creates one automatically: key ollama-local, label Local Ollama, kind ollama, base URL http://localhost:11434, model qwen2.5-coder:32b — disabled. The provider list marks it disabled: edit and save to enable; nothing is sent to it until an administrator points it at the real Ollama server and saves it.
  3. For any external provider: Allow external providers switched on. A provider is external when its kind is not ollama, or when it is an ollama provider whose base URL host is public or cannot be resolved (see What data is sent, and where).
  4. Optional: Allow read-only tool calls (mode C) for the tool lookups.

Until 1 and 2 hold — and 3 when the only usable provider is external — the Scout entry is not drawn in the sidebar at all, in any ADOM, even when Settings → Appearance → Sidebar menu has it ticked. The page still opens at /advisor/ and shows what is missing.

Permissions#

Action Needs
See Scout in the sidebar (once configured, see Requirements), chat, attach context, dismiss a proposal advisor.use
Apply as draft a WAF exception proposal advisor.use plus configuration-write — any of protection.edit, protection.apply, network.edit, operations.apply, appliances.edit or another key that grants it
Apply as draft a Lua script proposal advisor.use plus studio.lua_studio
Providers, API keys, the three switches, Test connection advisor.configure

The seeded operator profile includes advisor.use; the readonly profile does not, so read-only users do not see the menu entry and get 403 on /advisor/. advisor.configure is admin-only. Users without the proposal's apply permission get 403 when they click Apply as draft.

Conversations are private: you see your own. A user with users.manage can open anyone's conversation by its address.

How to use#

Set it up (administrator)#

  1. Go to Settings → AI → Scout → Providers (or click Configure on the Scout page).
  2. Under Providers, click Add provider, or Edit the seeded Local Ollama provider (marked disabled: edit and save to enable).
  3. Fill in Key (slug, unique), Label, Kind, Base URL, Model and, for external kinds, API key.
  4. Click Test connection — it sends one short request with the form's current values (nothing is saved) and shows the reply.
  5. Click Save. Saving a provider enables it. Use Make default on the provider new conversations should use.
  6. Switch on Enable Scout, and if needed Allow external providers and Allow read-only tool calls (mode C).

Ask a question#

  1. Open Operations → Troubleshooting → Scout in the sidebar.
  2. Click New conversation (or just type — a conversation is created on the first message).
  3. Optional: click the paperclip and choose Exceptions — <appliance> to attach that appliance's exception list.
  4. Type the question and press Enter or click Send (Shift+Enter inserts a new line).
  5. For an external provider, a confirmation shows the outbound text (first 600 characters), how many internal identifiers will be redacted (including those in earlier messages of the conversation) and how many earlier messages go along with it; click OK to send or Cancel to keep editing.
  6. While the reply streams, the bubble shows Thinking and any tool being run; click Stop to cancel.

Apply or dismiss a proposal#

  1. When a proposal card appears under the conversation, read the kind, title, rationale and JSON payload.
  2. Click Apply as draft or Dismiss. - A WAF exception becomes a row on the Exceptions page for that appliance. Pushing it to the device is still a separate step there. - A Lua script becomes a draft script in Lua Studio, linted like a typed one.

Configuration#

Field Description Required Example
Enable Scout Master switch; while off, sending is refused Yes on
Allow read-only tool calls (mode C) Lets the model request the read-only lookups No off
Allow external providers Required before any external provider is used (any non-ollama kind, or an ollama provider on a public or unresolvable host) For external providers off
Key (slug, unique) Provider identifier; cannot be changed when editing Yes corp-gateway
Label Display name No Corporate LLM gateway
Kind Ollama (local, no API key), OpenAI-compatible (ChatGPT / Azure OpenAI / LiteLLM / vLLM…), Anthropic (Claude Messages API) Yes OpenAI-compatible
Base URL Provider endpoint Yes https://llm.example.com/v1
Model Model name at that endpoint Yes gpt-4o-mini
API key Stored encrypted; blank keeps the existing key External kinds —

What data is sent, and where#

Situation What leaves SATOM
Local provider: kind ollama whose base URL host is localhost or a loopback, link-local or private address Your message, attachments, recent conversation history and (if enabled) tool results are sent unredacted to the Ollama base URL.
External provider: any other kind, or an ollama provider whose base URL host is public or cannot be resolved The same content, sent to the provider's base URL. Your new message, its attachments, any tool results and every earlier message sent along as history (up to 19, yours and the model's) are first passed through SATOM's identifier-redaction rules; the confirmation shows the result, the redaction count and how many earlier messages go along before sending. The call needs Allow external providers and is recorded in the export log.
Every exchange The model also receives SATOM's fixed system instructions. Attachments and tool results are wrapped in <<<UNTRUSTED>>> markers with an instruction never to follow commands found inside them.

⚠️Warning — Know what redaction covers

The built-in redaction rules replace private IPv4 addresses (10.x, 172.16–31.x, 192.168.x) and personal webmail addresses. Hostnames, device names and anything else are only redacted if your installation has additional publication rules. Earlier messages of the same conversation are re-sent as history with every new message; for an external provider they pass through the same rules, so anything the rules do not cover goes out again with each message.

ℹ️Note

Changed in 2.11.0: earlier messages sent as history to an external provider are now redacted too; an ollama provider on a public or unresolvable host is treated as external (redaction, Allow external providers, export log) by the assistant and by document translation alike; and on a new installation the seeded Local Ollama provider points at http://localhost:11434 and stays disabled until an administrator saves it.

The same providers, and the same local/external rule, serve document translation for change requests and the exception assistant: an ollama provider on a public host needs Allow external providers there too, and a disabled provider is refused by all of them.

Example#

🧪Example — Drafting a carve-out from a pasted block

An operator pastes a FortiWeb attack-log line and asks "Is this a false positive? What exception would you add?". The reply explains the signature and ends with a proposal card waf_exception — Allow ticket drafts. A user holding protection.edit clicks Apply as draft; the exception appears on the Exceptions page for that appliance, not yet pushed.

Result#

  • Every message is stored in the conversation, with duration, token counts and the tools used.
  • Every provider call — local or external, successful, failed or stopped — is recorded in the request ledger; calls to external providers are also recorded in an export log (provider, destination, bytes sent, redaction count).
  • Audit log entries: advisor.send per exchange, advisor.proposal_apply and advisor.proposal_dismiss. See Audit log.
  • A stopped reply keeps the text generated so far, marked stopped by you.

Troubleshooting#

"Scout is disabled — enable it in Settings → AI → Scout → Providers"#

Possible causes - Enable Scout is off. The page also shows a Disabled badge with Scout is turned off.

Solution 1. An administrator switches it on in Settings → AI → Scout → Providers.

"no AI provider configured -- add one in Settings -> Scout"#

Possible causes - No provider exists (the page shows No provider), or the conversation's provider was deleted and no default remains.

Solution 1. Add a provider and click Make default.

"the AI provider "Local Ollama" is disabled -- review its base URL and model in Settings -> Scout and save it to enable it"#

Possible causes - The conversation's provider is the seeded Local Ollama provider (or another provider marked disabled), which has not been reviewed and saved yet. Document translation reports the same condition as the AI provider is disabled.

Solution 1. In Settings → AI → Scout → Providers, click Edit on the provider, set the real Base URL and Model, click Test connection, then Save.

Verification - The provider no longer shows the disabled badge and a message gets a reply.

"external providers are disabled -- turn on "Allow external providers" in Settings -> Scout first"#

Possible causes - The conversation uses an openai or anthropic provider, or an ollama provider whose base URL host is public or cannot be resolved, and the external switch is off. Configuring a provider does not authorise traffic to it.

Solution 1. Switch on Allow external providers, or make an ollama provider on a local address (localhost, loopback, link-local or private) the default and start a new conversation.

Verification - Sending shows the external-provider confirmation instead of the error.

The first reply takes a minute or more, or times out#

Possible causes - A large local model is being loaded into memory on a cold call. Provider calls wait up to 180 seconds.

Solution 1. Wait — the elapsed time is shown in the reply bubble. Send again once the model is loaded.

The reply describes a change but no proposal card appears#

Possible causes - The model's proposal did not validate (unknown exception type, missing fields, missing Lua name or code). Invalid proposals are silently discarded; the reply itself is kept. - The reply was stopped — stopped replies never create proposals.

Solution 1. Ask the model to restate the proposal in the required satom-proposal format.

"Apply as draft" is refused#

Possible causes - 403: you lack the permission the manual form requires (configuration-write for an exception, studio.lua_studio for Lua). - proposal already applied / proposal already dismissed. - The target web protection profile is managed by a template; the lock message is shown and the proposal must be re-pointed at a cloned profile.

Tools never run#

Possible causes - Allow read-only tool calls (mode C) is off — the model is then not told the tools exist.

Solution 1. An administrator switches it on.

Advanced#

Advanced Tool lookups (mode C)

The model may request list_appliances, list_server_policies, device_health, list_probes, recent_config_changes, sot_search, list_exceptions and list_lua_scripts. All read SATOM's database and caches — never an appliance — and are limited to appliances visible to the user in the current ADOM. At most 4 tool rounds run per message; each result is capped at 8,000 bytes and marked when truncated.

Advanced Endpoints

/advisor/ (page), POST /advisor/new, POST /advisor/<id>/preview (what would be sent), POST /advisor/<id>/send-stream (streamed reply), POST /advisor/<id>/send (blocking reply), GET /advisor/usage (request ledger as JSON — your own calls, or everyone's with users.manage), GET /advisor/tools (tool catalog). Configuration endpoints live under /settings/ai/… and require advisor.configure.

Advanced Storage

Provider metadata is stored in application settings; API keys are stored encrypted per provider and never shown again. Conversations, messages, proposals, the request ledger and the export log are database tables. A conversation is scoped to the ADOM it was created in.
